card: Fixes a test flaw in p2p_eviction.py where the test passed even when block-time eviction protection was disabled or bypassed. Because block-relaying peers were connected first, fallback logic in CompareNodeBlockTime protected them as the oldest connections anyway. The test now connects eviction candidate peers first with lower mocktime ping responses so block and transaction protection steps are genuinely required. Test-only change.
changed_since_previous: No structural changes; the implementation maintains the approach of connecting eviction candidates first with mocktime-based ping delays.
evidence: PR description: "This can be shown by deleting the line where the peers send their block (L71 on master): block_peer.send_blocks_and_test([block], node, success=True)" and the test continues to pass.
problem: `p2p_eviction.py` passes even if block-time eviction protection is broken or completely disabled. Because block-sending peers were connected first, fallback logic in `CompareNodeBlockTime` protected them as the oldest inbound connections regardless of whether they sent blocks.

risk.why: A mistake can only cause functional test failures or CI flakiness.

summary: Restructures peer connection order and ping timings in the `p2p_eviction.py` functional test so that peer eviction protection for block-relaying peers is actually exercised. Eviction candidates are connected first and assigned lower ping times than block and transaction relayers using mocktime-controlled pong responses.
